entries.guidance: Named module-level classes compile inside callbacks: constructors, public fields and typed parameter properties, methods, lexical this in arrows, static members, named inheritance, super and instanceof. Instances share object identity; JSON and clone boundaries expose only own fields and drop class identity. See config-api.md for initialization, inference and refusal limits.
Use concrete named classes with public fields and methods. See config-api.md for the supported surface.

entries.message: package is not installed in node_modules
entries.guidance: Install the package with your package manager. Zero reads supported local TypeScript/ESM sources; it does not install packages or execute JavaScript.

Locally installed source packages resolve through nearest node_modules: exact exports with import/default conditions, module entries, and supported main/index entries. Scoped packages and exact exported subpaths are supported. The CommonJS subset accepts one static top-level function export; require, named CommonJS exports, implicit sloppy arguments, Node built-ins, export patterns, package aliases, declaration-only entries and package-target escapes are refused. Raw JavaScript uses checked runtime operations; TypeScript keeps static checking. Resolving a package does not establish compatibility with its host APIs or every export. Pinned npm probes compare selected real imports to Node.

Raw .js/.mjs/.cjs functions compile supported property access, calls, mutations and coercions through checked PHP dispatch. Missing values preserve undefined identity, invalid methods and null receivers throw TypeError, and TypeScript unknown still requires refinement. This supplies no Node/browser APIs, arbitrary prototypes, accessors, sparse arrays or custom iterators. The pinned npm matrix separately qualifies selected original library algorithms and combinations.
Use the clock in a handler or timestamp().defaultNow(). Configuration evaluation stays pure.
Return a row filter; put database effects in a hook or action.

entries.message: width must be an integer from 1 to 100
entries.guidance: Use an integer percentage from 1 to 100 for .ui({ width }).

Explicit undefined preserves typeof, coercion and JSON omission in compiled PHP. Some statically typed missing reads and annotation-only undefined/void still normalize to null; raw imported JavaScript uses a distinct undefined sentinel. The differential oracle normalizes final undefined results explicitly.

Configuration evaluation and compiled PHP index and slice strings in UTF-16 code units, like JS. A result that would split a surrogate pair is refused at build time or throws a RangeError at runtime, because UTF-8 cannot represent a lone surrogate. Diagnostic columns also count UTF-16 code units.

encodeURI and encodeURIComponent accept one string in configuration and handlers. Component punctuation is preserved; whole-URI delimiters are preserved only by encodeURI. Values must be valid Unicode scalar strings.
Field .ui() metadata survives nested schema emission and schema description and maps to native SCF. It does not affect data paths, validation or access.

Finite object interface inheritance and intersections, generic aliases/interfaces with constraints and defaults, finite keyof/indexed access and dynamic key reads, mapped types and selected utility/conditional types retain literal and optional boundaries. Concrete aliases also preserve class identity, typed fields/constructor parameter properties and method results while generated clients erase methods at the wire boundary. See runtime-contract.md (TypeScript type normalization) for the supported domains and refusals; the strict type-semantics fixture also checks generated-client boundaries and native/WASM parity.

Synchronous concrete helpers and inline callbacks can return named-parameter type predicates. The target must be a subtype of the parameter and the body must return booleans. Calls narrow their checked argument on the true branch; filter, find and findLast narrow elements when their first callback parameter is refined. Function aliases preserve predicates; map produces booleans. As in TypeScript, the authored predicate declares the refinement; the compiler does not prove nested runtime checks. Assertions, this predicates and predicate function-type annotations are refused. Direct Boolean callbacks retain JavaScript truthiness. Required tuple destructuring positions retain their declared types; array positions may be undefined, and mutation widens tuple read views. The type-semantics fixture checks native/WASM emission and strict client types.
A finite keyof is a literal union, not string.
Generic arguments must satisfy their declared structural constraints.
Provide every required argument; missing arguments never widen to unknown.
An indexed key must exist in every member of an object union.
Use an explicit string key type for open maps. Array/prototype and symbol key spaces are not modeled.
Recursive types are refused by bounded expansion; type operations also have a step and finite-key budget.
Use generic aliases with concrete PHP-reachable function signatures. There is no generic runtime specialization.
Record with finite string keys requires every declared key; it is not an open string map.
Conditional matching of primitive/array prototype properties is refused; use concrete scalar, array or finite object comparisons.
Combine interface declarations explicitly or use interface extends. Repeated declarations never silently replace earlier fields.

Use direct type parameters for distributive checks, or tuple-wrap alias/type-operation checks to make non-distributivity explicit. Alias reduction can otherwise change TypeScript distributivity before instantiation.

Use direct keyof T, a direct key parameter constrained by keyof T, or literal key domains. Aliased or reduced mapped key expressions (including Keys<T>, Identity<K> and keyof T | never) are refused before shape emission because reduction can change optional presence. Aliased or reduced key-parameter constraints are also refused.

Equality and inequality comparisons of typeof with number, string or boolean narrow unknown values and known scalar unions, including reversed operand order, property paths, conjunctions and early returns. False branches remove matching known union members; the complement of unknown remains unknown. Object, function, symbol, bigint and undefined guard domains are not added. The type-semantics fixture checks identical native/WASM output and strict generated-client types.

Global isFinite accepts zero or one argument and applies numeric coercion; Number.isFinite checks numbers without coercion. Number.isFinite is available as a stable function value, including local and captured aliases and feature detection. The differential numeric owner compares NaN, infinities, numbers, strings, null, booleans and arrays in pure configuration evaluation and PHP. Missing reads, built-in results and explicit undefined preserve their identity separately from null.

Typed `Map<K, V>`, `Set<T>`, `ReadonlyMap` and `ReadonlySet` compile to `Zero\JsMap`/`Zero\JsSet`: insertion order, SameValueZero keys (NaN equals NaN, -0 is +0), object keys by identity, and O(1) lookup. get/set/has/delete/clear/size/forEach, keys/values/entries, for...of, spread, Array.from and array-pattern destructuring follow JavaScript's live iteration: entries added during iteration are visited, deleted ones are skipped. An empty `new Map()`/`new Set()` needs type arguments. Module-level `new Map(entries)`/`new Set(values)` of static data are built once during configuration evaluation, which can read them with has/get/size but not mutate them, and compiled code captures one shared collection per request. Type arguments are invariant, because both collections are mutable. Calling `next()` on an iterator by hand is refused in typed code but supported in checked JavaScript, which also covers array keys/values/entries. Set algebra methods and Map getOrInsert are refused.

src/builtins.rs owns JavaScript built-in overloads, arity and phase support. Unsupported arguments are refused at the call site; runtime-only dynamic receivers throw a TypeError. Captured and runtime vectors compare UTF-16 ordering, replacement substitution, ECMAScript whitespace, modulo radix conversion and signed-zero rounding to Node. Positioned includes/startsWith/endsWith are refused in typed code and configuration evaluation; checked imported JavaScript implements those positions. Callback thisArg and nondecimal numeric toString are refused. Object.freeze is refused because freezing is not modeled. JSON parsing/serialization and Error construction are runtime-only; configuration evaluation refuses them. Custom object and function coercion are refused during configuration evaluation; handlers use the checked runtime conversion path. parseInt supports correctly rounded large values in base 10 and power-of-two bases; other radices require safe integer results. Database builders, configuration/schema factories and column modifiers share the source arity contract. Build-time function-coercion refusals include extracted methods; typed replacement callbacks preserve undefined captures and receive named groups. Captured explicit undefined remains distinct from null in both language modes. Dynamic method values use the shared built-in contract. Unknown built-in properties are refused during configuration evaluation. Powers accept safe integer results, integral binary scaling, squares, square roots and IEEE special values; other powers are refused at source or explicitly at runtime. Prototype setter literals are refused; computed __proto__ data properties remain supported. Extracted method calls are refused during configuration evaluation. Database writes require static collection references. Configuration for-of and destructuring use live iterators. Addition uses default primitive conversion. Sorting keeps undefined last and excludes it from comparators. JSON schemas must accept serialized values, and custom toJSON callbacks are refused. Typed Dates require explicit toISOString/toJSON before JSON.stringify or action returns. Imported JavaScript for-of uses live iterators. Ignore-case regexes require literal ASCII source and ASCII input in both modes; non-ASCII folding and encoded character escapes are refused. RegExp source and string conversion escape delimiters and line terminators. Regex split on astral text requires the u flag. Astral pattern literals and surrogate escapes also require u, even for ASCII/BMP subjects. Lone surrogate escapes in classes are refused; valid surrogate pairs and braced scalar escapes remain supported in Unicode mode. Typed invalid-Date toJSON returns null. Generated undefined defaults become null at the storage boundary. Object overwrites preserve key order. Stored JSON defaults omit undefined object properties and normalize undefined array slots to null. Numeric string conversion uses ECMAScript shortest ties-to-even formatting. Nullish narrowing retains undefined. Cyclic array string conversion omits recursive visits. Dynamic array/arguments prototype writes are refused. Typed Date string coercion requires explicit formatting. Function call/apply property values use the function contract; unmodeled function metadata/bind reads and function string conversion are refused. Optional Error/RegExp reads preserve undefined. Date construction runs default-hint object coercion. Typed Date addition/concat requires explicit formatting. Typed and imported Dates share JsDate identity and numeric primitive conversion; timestamp/date storage and filters convert explicitly. Date JSON schemas must describe their serialized text/null form. Non-ISO Date syntax receives a source diagnostic for literals and an explicit runtime refusal for computed values. Default sorting of multiple object values requires an explicit comparator; singleton sorting does not coerce. Negative-zero expanded Date years are refused. Custom sorting accepts only a numeric difference between the two parameters or matching property paths, with finite primitive keys. Other comparator shapes and cross-family borrowed methods are refused. Unary minus performs ToNumber, and parsed JSON retains negative zero. Missing indexed and optional-property logical assignment operands retain undefined in runtime narrowing and serialized client types. Regex source escaping uses explicit UTF-8 regardless of ambient PHP multibyte settings. Configuration refuses extracted built-in method values, including identity comparisons; direct and computed receiver calls remain supported. JSON negative-zero preservation leaves exponent signs intact. Non-Unicode regex classes support digit/underscore control escapes. Runtime hasIndices and unicodeSets are false because d/v flags are refused. Runtime Error messages are own nonenumerable properties only when a defined message is supplied; name is inherited. Configuration refuses restricted arguments access instead of fabricating native Error descriptors. Error stack metadata is refused. Captured arrays and objects retain one identity across typed and imported JavaScript. Capturing lookbehind is refused because JavaScript matches captures backward. Quantified noncapturing groups require a provably nonempty body; nullable groups are refused because regex engines choose different empty iterations. JavaScript-invalid regex literals receive syntax diagnostics before lowering. Runtime constructors refuse unsupported quantifier chains. Legacy class identity escapes preserve subsequent members. Undefined becomes null at schema-shaped storage boundaries, while required fields still reject null. Unicode regex property escapes are refused because PCRE and JavaScript use different Unicode databases; use explicit character classes. Character-class escapes next to unescaped hyphens are refused; escape literal hyphens. Date strings accept ISO syntax without space/compact-offset extensions, and time requires a complete date. Typed flat accepts depths 0 and 1 (null selects 0; undefined defaults to 1), with depth-specific element inference; checked imported JavaScript supports computed depths. Configuration typeof classifies Math, JSON and console as objects; host-dependent process/require/globalThis/crypto detection is refused. Lexical for headers retain per-iteration bindings during configuration evaluation. Runtime closures must be created after the lexical bindings they capture are initialized; forward captures are refused instead of resolving an outer binding. Named callbacks may omit only parameters that accept undefined; null does not allow omission. Lexical reads and assignments before initialization refuse at source in configuration and handlers, including for/of/in source expressions; parameter defaults cannot consume a later uninitialized parameter. Error cause options are refused whether cause is own data or an inherited class method. Captured closures use closure-object identity rather than function syntax for helper/type/wrapper caches, preserving distinct factory environments. Reassigning a named exported binding is refused at the write, preventing stale import snapshots while retaining stable let/var export aliases. This includes export aliases and named default exports. Const object identity and default-export expression snapshots retain JavaScript behavior. Lexical declarations directly under switch cases require explicit braces; shared switch lexical environments are refused. Checked JavaScript class-method reads and calls are explicitly refused instead of fabricating undefined or falling through to native methods. Typed array calls require native methods: own overrides installed by JavaScript receive an explicit runtime refusal before arguments run; checked JavaScript retains override dispatch. Runtime for-in snapshots keys and skips deleted properties. For-of lexical destructuring bindings are predeclared in each iteration before defaults run; earlier initialized bindings remain available. Configuration evaluation shares the handler refusal of destructured var loops. Computed data-method calls retain their receiver and resolve the callee before arguments. Named function expressions are refused at source because their private self-binding is not modeled; use anonymous expressions or function declarations.

Locale collation depends on the host and cannot be reproduced deterministically. localeCompare is refused in configuration and typed handlers; checked imported JavaScript throws TypeError. Use < or > for deterministic UTF-16 ordering. No byte-order substitute is exposed under the localeCompare name.

Optional chains support guarded property/index steps and single optional method calls. A non-optional continuation after a short-circuiting link is refused at source; guard each nullable step explicitly. Parenthesized chain boundaries retain ordinary property access and call behavior.

Defaults may reference earlier parameters. Closure defaults require a function body without new bindings and cannot refer to the current/later parameter. Classes and nested function creation in defaults are refused. These source diagnostics also cover nested destructuring defaults, preserving parameter initialization and closure scope.

undefined denotes the built-in missing value. Runtime bindings named undefined are refused at source, including function/class names, parameters, local declarations, imports, catch variables, loop variables and rest/destructuring bindings. Use a different local name.
